record.context_brief: Maximality of affine subgroup inside tame group
record.original_question: Let k be a field and let n > 2. Is the group Aff_n(k) a maximal subgroup of the tame transformation group TA_n(k)?

evidence.quote: Problem 6. Let k be a field. Is the group Affn(k), n > 2, a maximal subgroup of TAn(k) (tame transformation group)?

artifact.status_search_result: For $n=3$ over a field of characteristic zero, Edo and Furter proved that $\mathrm{Aff}_3(k)$ is not a maximal subgroup of $\mathrm{TA}_3(k)$, exhibiting proper intermediate subgroups generated by $\mathrm{Aff}_3(k)$ together with certain non-cotame tame automorphisms (the first such example was constructed by Edo–Lewis, 2015). For general $n>3$ and arbitrary fields, the question does not appear to be fully settled.

status_evidence.title: The Affine Automorphism Group of A^3 is Not a Maximal Subgroup of the Tame Automorphism Group
status_evidence.snippet: There exists a family of proper subgroups of the tame automorphism group of affine three-space generated by the affine subgroup and a non-affine tame automorphism.
status_evidence.claim: In characteristic zero, $\mathrm{Aff}_3$ is not a maximal subgroup of $\mathrm{TA}_3$.

status_evidence.title: Co-tame automorphisms (arXiv:1609.02670)
status_evidence.snippet: Edo–Lewis gave the first example of a non-cotame tame automorphism in three variables, showing the affine group together with this automorphism does not generate the full tame group.
status_evidence.claim: Non-cotame tame automorphisms exist for n=3, witnessing non-maximality.
